question: A team is designing a schema to extract a customer's phone number from scanned support emails. Many older emails in the corpus never mention a phone number at all. In an early version, phone_number was marked as a required string field, and the team noticed Claude sometimes fabricated plausible-looking numbers to satisfy the schema. What is the best fix?
options: A) Keep phone_number required but change its type from string to an enum of common area codes so the model has fewer values to guess from
B) Keep phone_number required and add a second required field called phone_number_confidence so low-confidence guesses can be filtered out later
C) Make phone_number an optional, nullable field so Claude can omit it or return null when the source document contains no phone number
D) Remove the tool definition entirely and ask Claude in plain prose to only include a phone number if it is confident one was found
correct_answers: C) Make phone_number an optional, nullable field so Claude can omit it or return null when the source document contains no phone number
explanations: An enum of area codes still forces the model to pick some value, and area codes don't even represent full phone numbers, so fabrication risk remains and the field's meaning becomes wrong.
Adding a confidence field doesn't change the fact that phone_number itself is still required, so the model is still forced to produce some value even when none exists in the source.
Correct. Designing fields as optional/nullable when source documents may not contain the information removes the pressure to fabricate a value just to satisfy a required-field constraint.
Dropping tool use altogether reintroduces JSON syntax risk and gives up the schema-compliance guarantees that tool use provides, trading one problem for a worse one.
